title: Automated Logistics Invoice Digitization
business: A regional logistics firm processing thousands of scanned freight invoices daily.
problem: Manual data entry teams struggle with inconsistent table layouts in scanned PDFs, leading to high error rates when extracting line-item costs and shipping weights.
solution: The Table Transformer (TATR) model identifies the spatial coordinates of rows, columns, and individual cells within document images, allowing the firm to programmatically isolate table regions for downstream OCR processing.
steps: Convert incoming PDF invoices into high-resolution image formats suitable for model input.
Pass the image through the Table Transformer to generate bounding box coordinates for table structures.
Apply non-maximum suppression to filter overlapping structure detections.
Crop the identified table regions and pass them to a secondary OCR engine for text extraction.
Map the extracted text to the identified row/column coordinates to reconstruct the structured data.
outcome: The firm achieves a more reliable transformation of unstructured document pixels into structured data formats, reducing the reliance on manual verification for standard invoice layouts.
limitation: The model is sensitive to image resolution and document orientation; if the scan is skewed or low-quality, the bounding box predictions may become misaligned, which can be checked by visualizing the predicted boxes against the original image.
